purpose: Compare B12X batched Kimi-K3 top-16 expert selection with paired projection gathering against paired gathering followed by the vLLM topk_sigmoid reference.

hardware.gpu_model: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition

command: docker run --gpus all --network host --ipc host --shm-size 32g --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 --entrypoint /bin/bash -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True -e NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 -e NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS -v $PWD:/work:ro -v $B12X_CACHE_DIR:/cache/jit -w /work voipmonitor/vllm:kimi-k3-ii-vllmf21a391-b12x3be8bc7-cu133-torch213-20260816-r2 -lc 'unset NCCL_GRAPH_FILE; export PYTHONPATH=/work:/opt/kimi-k3-qsrt/vllm:${PYTHONPATH:-}; /opt/venv/bin/python benchmarks/benchmark_kimi_k3_pair_topk.py --world-size 16 --batch 8 --topk-threads 256 --warmup 100000 --iterations 10000 --samples 5'

correctness.random: expert IDs, FP32 weights, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly
correctness.ties: expert IDs, FP32 weights, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly
correctness.near_ties: expert IDs, FP32 weights, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly
correctness.nonfinite_wide_range: expert IDs, FP32 weights, finite masks, nonzero masks, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly
correctness.all_negative_infinity: B12X returns 16 distinct in-range expert IDs per row; FP32 weights, finite masks, nonzero masks, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly; the vLLM reduction does not define which 16 experts win a complete tie
correctness.cuda_graph_replay: random-input expert IDs, FP32 weights, and gathered BF16 projection data match exactly

timing_microseconds.speedup_definition: reference_median / b12x_median; values greater than one mean the B12X path is faster

conclusion: The B12X batched operation is exact for defined expert-order cases, preserves distinct experts for a fully degenerate tie, satisfies CUDA Graph replay requirements, and reduces median TP16 batch-8 gather-plus-selection latency by 24.97 percent.
